translations.answer: The Sentis–Khatib framework places contact, joint-limit, and obstacle-avoidance constraints at the highest level, then projects operational-space tasks and postures through dynamically consistent null spaces. This gives multi-task WBC explicit priorities, but the original evidence is real-time simulation and does not replace hardware validation of friction cones, torque, latency, or contact switching.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: Robot dynamics, constraint Jacobians, and support-contact models are sufficiently accurate.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Rank, singularity, constraint violation, and degraded modes are monitored explicitly at runtime.
translations.applicability.environments.0: Real-time simulation with the paper's rigid-floor and high-friction assumptions.
translations.applicability.robots.0: Free-floating humanoid model; no hardware validation in the paper.
translations.applicability.simulators.0: No reproducible official public implementation is identified in the paper.
translations.confidence_rationale: The derivation and real-time simulations support the constraint–task–posture hierarchy. Confidence is capped because there is no quantitative hardware experiment or official code.
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines dynamically consistent null-space prioritization and demonstrates joint limits, obstacle avoidance, and free-floating support composition.
translations.evidence.0.title: A Whole-Body Control Framework for Humanoids Operating in Human Environments
translations.title: Why should multi-task WBC define constraint priorities before tuning a weighted sum?
